dedupe_keys.name: technology and facility level energy cost and environmental performance of u s industries chemicals cement iron and steel food

description: This Dryad dataset is a single JSON file that characterises existing U.S. industrial facilities and emerging production technologies for energy systems modelling. For six industries it lists existing facilities with location and process route: ammonia (36 facilities in 20 states), cement (97 facilities in 35 states, dry and wet kilns), ethanol (201 facilities), ethylene and propylene (35 facilities in six states, all steam cracking), iron and steel (102 facilities in 31 states, mostly electric arc furnaces) and food (production and energy intensity by state for five subsectors). It also parameterises emerging routes such as hydrogen direct reduction, carbon capture, electrified kilns and crackers, and heat pumps, and inventories 18 solutions for agriculture, mining and construction. An assumptions section fixes units, fuel and feedstock prices, plant cost indices and a 2018 dollar base. Version 6 was published on 4 November 2025 under CC0 and is about 6 MB; access is free. Sources are public (EPA GHGRP, USGS, EIA, industry reports and literature), with WGS84 coordinates. Caveats: emerging-technology figures come from literature and pilots, facility lists reflect one snapshot, and costs are normalised estimates, not plant accounts. For simulation it gives facility locations, capacities and energy intensities for capacity planning, decarbonisation pathway and energy demand models of heavy industry. Related catalogue records include the EPA Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program, the Global Cement and Concrete Tracker and the EIA Manufacturing Energy Consumption Survey.
